# Scenix v1.8.0 — Terrain, Sky, And Water

Scenix `1.8.0` adds three optional, `no_std`-capable CPU crates for real-world
environments — `scenix-terrain` (heightmaps, chunked LOD, splats, collision,
streaming), `scenix-sky` (procedural atmosphere, sun positions, baked
environment maps), and `scenix-water` (Gerstner waves, foam, fresnel,
underwater tinting, mirror/reflection helpers) — plus a GPU environment draw
path in `scenix-renderer` behind its `environment` feature, material
descriptors in `scenix-material`, and the schema ids in `scenix-core`.
Everything is additive and feature-gated; the default facade build behaves
exactly like v1.7.0.

## Highlights

- `scenix-terrain` is a standalone CPU crate (`std`/`serde`): deterministic
  seeded `Heightmap::from_noise` (raw noise stays in `[-1, 1]`,
  `remap_range` refits spans), `TerrainGrid::generate` chunking with
  `TerrainConfig` (chunks per axis × chunk cells × `LodPolicy` bands),
  per-LOD `chunk_geometry` plus `chunk_geometry_with_splat` that packs
  normalized splat weights into vertex color channels, `SplatMap` lattice
  math, `TerrainCollider` ray probes (`with_step`, `with_max_steps`,
  `height_at`, unit-length `normal_at`), and a deterministic
  `ChunkStreamer` poll/unload loop over wrapping lattices.
- `scenix-sky` profiles produce pure direction-tap colors:
  `SkyModel::clear_day`/`overcast_haze` with a turbidity/rayleigh/mie tuning
  surface; `SunPosition` translates elevation/azimuth into unit-length sun
  directions and drives `SunLight`/`DirectionalLight` (warm low sun, neutral
  zenith); `bake_equirectangular` produces deterministic sky maps with the
  v = 0 zenith baking convention, `bake_light_probe` projects radiance into
  sh_coefficients taps, and `bake_ambient` collapses the map into sky/ground
  hemisphere averages; `GroundedSkybox` fades a dome into a flat ground
  patch under the horizon line.
- `scenix-water` simulates on the CPU as the source of truth:
  `WaveField` presets (`ocean_shore`, `calm`) hold up to MAX_WAVES (4)
  stacked `GerstnerWave`s (`wave_number = 2pi/wavelength`, deep-water
  `phase_speed`); `WaterSurface::geometry(t)` builds displaced meshes whose
  vertices match `height_at` exactly, with unit-length normals;
  `FoamParams::shoreline` gates crest energy behind a hard threshold;
  `FresnelParams::water` follows Schlick reflectance (grazing angles mirror
  fully); `UnderwaterView` tints with red-first absorption and distance
  murk drift; `mirror_transform`/`reflected_camera` build the reflection
  math for planar water reflections.
- `scenix-material` adds self-contained `TerrainMaterial` (four splat
  layers with albedo/roughness/tiling plus optional splat and detail
  textures), `SkyMaterial` (gradient triple, direction/color/glare sun
  params, fade band, atmosphere flag), and `WaterMaterial` (deep/shallow
  tints, Schlick base reflectance, optional foam threshold/sharpness,
  optional reflection/refraction textures), plus `ShaderKind::Terrain`,
  `ShaderKind::Sky`, `ShaderKind::Water` variants and the
  `FEATURE_SPLAT_MAP` (1 << 22), `FEATURE_ATMOSPHERE` (1 << 23),
  `FEATURE_FRESNEL` (1 << 24), `FEATURE_FOAM` (1 << 25), and
  `FEATURE_REFRACTION` (1 << 26) bits.
- `scenix-renderer` (behind `renderer` + `environment`) owns an environment
  registry keyed by node material ids: `register_environment` upserts a slot
  from `EnvironmentMaterial::Terrain/Sky/Water` (terrain gets pre-packed
  chunk geometry; water gets the `WaveField` the GPU paver replays), three
  WGSL pipelines run per frame — splat weights from vertex channels or the
  splat texture, a depth-no-write sky dome, and an alpha-blended water
  surface that displaces with the same GPU Gems wave math as the CPU —
  with sky-before-opaque and water-after-transparent draw ordering, an
  environment uniform belt, and dynamic bind groups rebuilt only on
  registration changes.
- `scenix-core` adds the `TerrainId`, `SkyId`, and `WaterId` newtypes;
  `scenix-scene` adds `NodeKind::Terrain/Sky/Water` nodes whose material
  link drives slot lookup at draw time.
- `scenix-texture` adds `EquirectSampler` (bilinear sampling over an
  equirectangular map in the sky-bake row order) and `height_to_normal_map`
  (central-difference height-to-normal conversion) for environment
  tooling.
- `scenix-wasm` documents the browser fallback plan:
  `environment_fallback_plan(WebGlCapabilityLevel)` — WebGPU gets full WGSL
  parity with reflection/refraction targets, WebGL 2 renders with static
  per-slot uniforms (screen-space water survives via framebuffers), and
  WebGL 1 falls back to CPU-baked vertex-color tinting without
  screen-space water.
- The facade gains `terrain`, `sky`, `water`, and `environment` features
  (terrain and sky re-export lists are curated because the `lod`/`sky`/`sun`
  module names collide with the scene, material, and light glob re-exports).

## Small Example

```rust
use scenix::{EnvironmentMaterial, MaterialId, Renderer, RendererConfig, SceneGraph, SceneNode};
use scenix::{SkyId, SkyMaterial, TerrainId, TerrainMaterial, WaterId, WaterMaterial};
use scenix::{Heightmap, LodBand, LodPolicy, TerrainConfig, TerrainGrid};

let mut renderer = Renderer::headless(RendererConfig::new(320, 240)).await?;

// 1. Terrain: a small two-chunk heightfield at LOD 0.
let map = Heightmap::from_fn(17, 17, 1.0, |ix, iz| ((ix + iz) as f32) * 0.5);
let policy = LodPolicy::new(&[LodBand::new(40.0, 0)])?;
let chunk = TerrainGrid::generate(&map, TerrainConfig::new(2, 8, policy))
    .chunk_geometry(0, 0)?;

let terrain = TerrainMaterial::default_palette();
renderer.register_environment(
    MaterialId::new(1),
    EnvironmentMaterial::Terrain(&terrain, &chunk),
)?;

// 2. Sky: a procedural dominating dome.
let sky = SkyMaterial::clear_day();
renderer.register_environment(MaterialId::new(2), EnvironmentMaterial::Sky(&sky))?;

// 3. Scene nodes key the slots through the schema.
let mut scene = SceneGraph::new();
scene.add(SceneNode::terrain("hills", TerrainId::new(1), MaterialId::new(1)));
scene.add(SceneNode::sky("backdrop", SkyId::new(1), MaterialId::new(2)));
scene.update_world_transforms();

// stats.scene_environments / stats.visible_environments are reported per
// frame; FrameStats has no post-condition on culling counts.
```

Feature gates: `environment` (terrain + sky + water), `renderer` + `environment`
for the GPU draw path, `material` for the descriptors (default-on in the
facade), and `scene` for the node schema (default-on).
